msg: Colors matter, but you have to be able to adapt and switch to the other color in the pair once the amount of mushrooms start going down. My experience was that the red toned colors paid out the most at first (red, purple, pink, brown) and then after a couple rounds one of them would pay out very low or zero. That is when you switch to the other set of 4 colors (blue, green, yellow, orange) and repeat the previous process until one of those colors pays out either zero or very low. Low meaning below 4 mushrooms. The gnomes will always come out together in the same color pairs so you won't be scrambling to pick some mystery pair. The 2 different forests didn't really seem to matter as far as I could tell. You could get 9 in either of them, and 9 is the most I ever got so I believe that's the maximum you can get per round. I didn't really notice anything with the color baskets you get in each round. I believe the color of the gnome is the main deciding factor on how many mushrooms you get. If you can separate the red toned colors from the rest of the gnome colors and be able to understand that it's time to choose the other set of 4 colors for a while I believe you will do well.
